subject: POC qualification & execution outline for ClearLedger
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@clearledger.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC qualification & execution outline for ClearLedger

Alyssa — thanks again for the call earlier. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the sandbox POC. I tried to keep the ask measurable (so we can gate).

Summary of needs from ClearLedger
- Primary use case: document ingestion + question-answering for mortgage underwriting docs (batch + interactive).
- Target throughput: bursts up to ~50 req/s for search+generate flows; steady-state ~10 rps.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile end-to-end < 350ms for 256-token responses; p99 < 600ms for typical queries.
- Cost sensitivity: target compute-only cost <= $0.0015 per token for production unit economics.
- Quality signals: human review precision >= 88% on a 200-sample prompt set; hallucinations < 3% on sampled queries.

Proposed POC scope (2-week sandbox)
1) Week 0 (prep) — exchange sample workload, credentials, and success criteria; Redwood delivers a baseline config and estimated cost profile.
2) Week 1 (smoke + perf) — run a 24-hour smoke with 5k sample queries from your dataset; capture latency/throughput/cost.
3) Week 2 (quality + ops) — run human eval on 200-sample set, tuning prompts and quantization as needed; produce final performance and cost report.

Owners & explicit asks
- ClearLedger: provide canonical sample workload (PDFs + ingestion CSV), a 200-sample QA set with expected answers, and any redaction rules. (Alyssa / Ben)
- Redwood infra lead (Karthik): will provision the sandbox cluster, attach telemetry, and run perf smoke.
- Redwood CS (Monica): will coordinate human eval schedule and provide the eval rubric template.
- Redwood AE (Jordan): oversee timeline, commercial questions, and final handoff.

Acceptance criteria (must be met to consider POC successful)
- Latency: p95 < 350ms on the 256-token standard query shape; p99 < 600ms.
- Throughput: sustain 10 rps steady with bursts up to 50 rps without >5% error rate.
- Cost: compute-only token cost estimate <= $0.0015/token with suggested configs.
- Quality: human eval precision >= 88% and hallucination rate < 3% on the agreed sample.

Next steps (please confirm by EOD tomorrow so we can provision)
1) ClearLedger to drop the sample workload and 200-sample eval into the Drive link below.
2) Redwood to share a mutual action plan (MAP) and a provisional infra quote.
3) Schedule kickoff (30–45 mins) for Monday to walk through telemetry and runbook.

Drive (placeholders): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cClearLedgerPOC

Thanks — I’ll pause provisioning until we have the sample data and you confirm acceptance criteria.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Date: 2026-05-24T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC qualification & execution outline for ClearLedger

Jordan — appreciate the tight recap. This aligns mostly with what we discussed. A few clarifications and small asks from our side: 

1) Latency targets: can we make the p99 target softer for the initial sandbox (p99 < 800ms) with an expectation to tighten in production? We’re ok with a stricter p95 as the priority.
2) Throughput: the 50 rps burst is expected during nightly batch ingest windows. We need a runbook for graceful degradation if token cost spikes.
3) Quality: the 200-sample set is ready; I’ll upload with expected answers. However, our compliance team also requires logging of request/response hashes and retention policy details before we run any data. Can you confirm what telemetry will be stored and for how long?

We can provide the dataset and the 200-sample eval by Friday COB. Kickoff Monday works — suggest 10:30 PDT.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Morgan
Head of Data & Automation | ClearLedger
alyssa@clearledger.com

Attachment: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@clearledger.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-25T00:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC qualification & execution outline for ClearLedger

Thanks — quick technical notes so expectations are clear before we spin up the sandbox: 

- Telemetry & retention: by default sandbox telemetry will include request/response timing, per-token counts, and anonymized request hashes; we can enable full request/response logging on a short-term basis behind your consent. Retention in the sandbox will be 30 days unless you request otherwise. For Private (prod) we support customer-controlled KMS and configurable retention.
- Cost estimate: baseline run (1 GPU, int8 quantized model variant, 2k sample queries/day) is estimated at ~$0.0012/token compute-only; perf tuning for latency may increase cost ~8–15% depending on batch sizing.
- Perf note: to hit p95 < 350ms consistently we’ll likely use a smaller context window and prefer model variant A (optimized kernels). I’ll attach a short perf summary and a sample-workload manifest schema so you can confirm the query shapes.

I’ve attached the preliminary latency summary and a sample workload YAML. Monica — once the 200-sample set is uploaded, we can start the smoke runs and schedule the human eval slots.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Platform Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Perfect — thanks for the quick replies. Confirming the operational plan: 

- Alyssa/Ben: upload the sample workload + 200-sample eval to the Drive folder by Friday COB. Also include any compliance constraints (redaction rules, retention window).
- Karthik: provision the 1-GPU sandbox, enable telemetry as discussed (30-day retention), and run the 24-hour smoke on Monday afternoon PST. Share the perf dashboard link when available.
- Monica: propose two human-eval windows (Tues/Wed) for reviewers; we’ll run the 200-sample set through the rubric and capture precision/hallucination metrics.

I’ll book the Monday kickoff for 10:30 PDT and send a calendar invite with the Drive and MAP attached. If any acceptance criteria are a hard no-go (e.g., cost threshold), flag them in the kickoff so we can discuss alternatives — quantization, batching, or model variant choices.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting this moving.

—Jordan
